power: Let power manager detect change to dark_resume pref dynamically. Several tests depend on RTC triggering a full wake. suspend_stress_test is one of them. Previously we used override dark_resume preference before the test. Thanks to b/132365846 we had to delete that code (crrev.com/c/1628588). Since restarting powerd makes CRAS fragile, we need powerd to detect changes to dark resume pref without having to restart. This change provides powerd the same capability. BUG=b:141459234 TEST=Check if powerd recognizes change to pref without restarting. Change-Id: I5c5ce7bed985fe12ac6161e697f6fd9a1d01b786 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1834651 Tested-by: Ravi Chandra Sadineni <ravisadineni@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Ravi Chandra Sadineni <ravisadineni@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Todd Broch <tbroch@chromium.org>

power: Disable dark resume on powerd_dbus_suspend. If dark resume is enabled on a given platform, keeping it enabled on test builds will help catch regressions more quickly. This also means dark resume will interfere with tests that use RTC to resume from suspend. Since the tests (autottests and suspend_stress_test) use powerd_dbus_suspend to trigger suspend/resume, disabling dark resume here (in powerd_dbus_suspend.cc) would make sure dark resume does not come in the path of resuming using RTC as part of tests. This change achives the same. BUG=b:141459234 TEST=Make sure 'powerd_dbus_suspend suspend_for_secs=10' causes full resume. Change-Id: Ia71bfd2e18bf078cc5eb05ac5032aeffa2e1f1c7 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1834652 Tested-by: Ravi Chandra Sadineni <ravisadineni@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Ravi Chandra Sadineni <ravisadineni@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Eric Caruso <ejcaruso@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Todd Broch <tbroch@chromium.org>

Remove dark resume preference setter for test images. Since the idea is to keep the dark resume setting to default so as to find regressions easily, this change removes the file that changes dark resume preference on the test images. The preference is overridden in powerd_dbus_suspend so as to prevent interference with autotests that use RTC to wakeup from suspend (crrev.com/c/1834652). chromeos-config: match ARM architecture more broadly veyron_mighty uses the architecture string "armv7l", which we did not account for in our list of machine types. More broadly match arm machine types by looking for "arm" or "aarch64" as the beginning of the string. The reason this matters is veyron_mighty, despite being non-unibuild, needs to fallback to mosys, and architecture detection needs to happen before mosys can be run. BUG=chromium:991653,chromium:1009475 TEST=sudo FEATURES=test emerge chromeos-config-tools TEST=cros_config /firmware image-name now runs "mosys platform model" on veyron_mighty instead of failing Change-Id: Iefa7f335f117b89894d6215bd0de75bd49a8d767 Signed-off-by: Jack Rosenthal <jrosenth@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1849427 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Abe Levkoy <alevkoy@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Simon Glass <sjg@chromium.org>
